title.narrative: Provision of lifesaving WASH services to rural communities likely to experience drought due to La NIna in Wamlawein district of Lower Shabelle region of South West State.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe acute malnutrition situation remains dire, with an estimated 1.2 million children under the age of five across Somalia facing acute malnutrition in 2024. South West State is particularly affected, showing some of the highest rates of malnutrition, with several districts expected to experience Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) rates above the emergency threshold of 15%. Health systems in the region are overwhelmed, with limited capacity to provide adequate nutrition and healthcare services. This is compounded by disease outbreaks such as cholera and measles, which further aggravate the nutritional status of already vulnerable populations, particularly children, pregnant and lactating women, and the elderly. The most recent situation report from UNOCHA (June 2024) highlights that humanitarian needs in South West State continue to rise, with over 3.9 million people in need of urgent assistance across Somalia. The impact of climate shocks, including recurrent droughts and erratic rainfall patterns, continues to devastate local agricultural production, livestock health, and water availability. This has significantly diminished livelihoods and increased displacement, further straining local communities and their coping mechanisms. The lack of access to clean water and adequate sanitation also worsens the risk of waterborne diseases, which disproportionately affect children and women. ltbrgtAs per the recent Greater Horn of Africa Climate Outlook Forum, Somalia is facing a 70 percent likelihood of La Niña, and the conditions may persist into 2025 with the most affected areas likely to be central and southern Somalia as well as parts of Puntland. Rural pastoral and agro-pastoral livelihoods are at risk of elevated food insecurity due to reduced access to water, low production, and limited income. Drought conditions will also impact scarce urban water supply systems, affecting urban and displaced populations in camp settings and heightening the risk of disease outbreak. Wanlaweyn is one of the top priority districts for implementing anticipatory actions to mitigate the scale of projected drought. Such earlier action measures can significantly reduce the adverse effects on the community. ltspangtNew Ways is proposing a 6-month integrated WASH project targeting the community likely to be affected La Nina in Wanlawein district reaching a total of 14,000 persons including (4,400 men, 6,000 women, 1,900 girls, and 1,700 boys). In this project, New Ways aims to improve access to life-saving WASH services for people living in Wanlawein district of Lower Shabelle region of South West State with recognition of people with disabilities, and the most vulnerable population. lt/spangtltspangtNew Ways Organization will undertake the following activities in this project:lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtConstruction of 100 normal latrines and 15 latrines for people living with disabilities to benefit residents in Wanlawein town and the rural areaslt/pgtltpgtHygiene promotions sessions will be conducted regularly and cleaning-up campaigns using the provided sanitation tools.lt/pgtltpgtProvision of safe drinking water to 3500 individuals through rehabilitation of shallow wells and construction of water tanks with water kiosksltbrgtDistribution of hygiene kits to 2000 Households.ltbrgt10 Hygiene promoters will be recruited and trainedltbrgtRehabilitation of 3 shallow wells and construction of 1 in the target locationslt/pgtltpgtMonitoring and Supervision exercise twice during the project periodltbrgt4 WASH committees will be established and trained to improve all preventive measures against the risks of AWD/cholera outbreaksltbrgtChlorination of the wells through recruited hygiene promoters i.e 10 shallow wells for the project period.ltbrgt60 packs of sanitation tools will be procured and distributed in the target locationsltbrgtConduct 1 post distribution monitoring exercise at the tail end of the projectltbrgtlt/pgt
